transcript.en: Hello English learners and welcome to another lesson with EnglishPod.
transcript.zh: 大家好，英语学习者们，欢迎来到 EnglishPod 的又一节课。

transcript.en: And today we're bringing you a great Christmas lesson.
transcript.zh: 今天我们为大家带来一节很棒的圣诞节课。

transcript.en: We've got a lot of Christmas vocabulary in today's lesson for you.
transcript.zh: 今天的课里有很多圣诞词汇要教给大家。

transcript.en: Yeah, it's almost Christmas time so everyone is getting into the spirit, especially here at EnglishPod, so we're going to teach you a little bit more about this.
transcript.zh: 是的，快到圣诞节了，大家都进入了节日氛围，尤其是在 EnglishPod，所以我们要多教你们一些这方面的知识。

transcript.en: Speaking of the spirit, I think it's time for us to look at our vocabulary preview.
transcript.zh: 说到节日氛围，我想是时候来看词汇预览了。

transcript.en: So in this part of our show, we'll look at some key language in the dialogue that you'll need to know to understand the dialogue.
transcript.zh: 在节目的这个部分，我们来看一些对话中的关键语言，你需要知道它们才能理解对话。

transcript.en: And actually today we only have one word.
So, eggnog is a really popular Christmas drink.
transcript.zh: 蛋奶酒是一种非常受欢迎的圣诞饮品。
是一种传统的圣诞饮品。

transcript.en: It's eggs, cream, sugar, and usually rum.
transcript.zh: 鸡蛋、奶油、糖，通常还有朗姆酒。

transcript.en: There's actually a drink very similar to this in Chile.
transcript.zh: 其实智利有一种非常类似的饮品。

transcript.en: So in Spanish that would be...
Yeah, so it's actually really, really good.
I mean, it's really similar to eggnog.
transcript.zh: 我是说，跟蛋奶酒非常像。

transcript.en: So with that in mind, let's take a listen to our dialogue for the first time.
transcript.zh: 带着这个认识，我们来听第一遍对话。

transcript.en: I hate working on Christmas Eve.
transcript.zh: 我真讨厌在平安夜上班。

transcript.en: Whoa, get a load of this guy.
I think we got ourselves a situation here.
Have you been drinking tonight, sir?
I had one or two glasses of eggnog, but nothing else.
transcript.zh: 我喝了一两杯蛋奶酒，别的没喝。

transcript.en: Step out of the vehicle, please.
Sir, what do you have in the back?

transcript.zh: 毕竟这是送礼的季节嘛。

transcript.en: Don't take that tone with me.
transcript.zh: 别用这种口气跟我说话。

transcript.en: Do you have an invoice for these items?
transcript.zh: 你有这些东西的发票吗？

transcript.en: I make these in my workshop in the North Pole.
transcript.zh: 这是我在北极的工作室里做的。

transcript.en: You have the right to remain silent.
Anything you say can and will be used against you.
transcript.zh: 你所说的一切都可能并且将会成为对你不利的证据。

transcript.en: You have the right to an attorney.
If you can't afford one, the state will appoint one for you.
transcript.zh: 如果你请不起，政府会为你指定一名。

transcript.en: Do you understand these rights that have just been read to you?
transcript.zh: 你明白刚才向你宣读的这些权利吗？

transcript.en: You can't take me to jail.

transcript.zh: 鲁道夫、普兰瑟、丹瑟，救命啊！

transcript.en: Well I did not see that one coming.
Santa Claus is being taken to jail.
transcript.zh: 圣诞老人被抓去坐牢了。

transcript.en: We'll talk about that in a little while.
Let's take a look at some language from this dialogue.
transcript.zh: 来看看这段对话中的一些语言。

transcript.en: So the first word that we have on our language takeaway today is vehicle.
transcript.zh: 今天语言要点的第一个词是 vehicle（交通工具）。

transcript.en: So all of those are vehicles.
transcript.zh: 所以这些全都是交通工具。

transcript.en: Now I thought that a vehicle was a car specifically.
transcript.zh: 我之前以为 vehicle 专门指汽车。

transcript.en: No, any machine that carries people from one place to another is a vehicle.
transcript.zh: 不，任何把人从一个地方运到另一个地方的机器都是 vehicle。

transcript.en: Let's take a look now at our second word.
Let's move to our third word which is appoint.
transcript.zh: 来看第三个词，appoint（指定/任命）。

transcript.en: Okay, so the president of a country might appoint his chief of staff.
transcript.zh: 好的，比如一国的总统可能会任命他的幕僚长。

transcript.en: Right, or I can appoint my attorney.
transcript.zh: 对，或者我可以指定我的律师。

transcript.en: So can you appoint a thing?
transcript.zh: 那你能任命一个东西吗？

transcript.en: Can I appoint my coffee cup?
transcript.zh: 我能任命我的咖啡杯吗？

transcript.en: You only use it for people.
Alright, let's move to our final word.
You can tell us about sleighs.
transcript.zh: 你可以给我们讲讲雪橇。

transcript.en: A sleigh is a vehicle that is pulled by a horse and travels over snow or ice.
transcript.zh: 雪橇是一种由马拉着的交通工具，在雪地或冰面上行驶。

transcript.en: So, you know, like Santa drives a sleigh.
transcript.zh: 你知道，就像圣诞老人驾着雪橇一样。

transcript.en: So do you drive a sleigh or ride a sleigh?
transcript.zh: 那你是 drive a sleigh 还是 ride a sleigh？

transcript.en: Well, the song says you ride in a one-horse open sleigh.
transcript.zh: 嗯，歌里唱的是「ride in a one-horse open sleigh」。

transcript.en: I think it's time for us to look at some interesting phrases that we found in this dialogue.
transcript.zh: 我想是时候来看看这段对话中的一些有趣短语了。

transcript.en: So let's look at putting it together.
Today on Putting it Together, we have two great phrases for you and let's take a look at the first one.
transcript.zh: 今天的整合运用，我们为大家准备了两个很棒的短语，先看第一个。

transcript.en: So step out means to go out of a place for a short period of time.
transcript.zh: Step out 意思是短暂地离开某个地方。

transcript.en: So in our dialogue, for example, the police officer said, step out of the vehicle.
transcript.zh: 比如在对话中，警察说：下车（step out of the vehicle）。

transcript.en: You can also say, step out of the office.
transcript.zh: 你也可以说，离开办公室一下。

transcript.en: You can say, I just stepped out of the shower.
transcript.zh: 你可以说，我刚从淋浴间出来。

transcript.en: Now, we can also say, step in.
transcript.zh: 我们也可以说 step in（进去）。

transcript.en: I can ask Marco, step into my office for a moment.
transcript.zh: 我可以跟马可说，进我办公室来一下。

transcript.en: So that's step out and step in.
transcript.zh: 所以这就是 step out 和 step in。

transcript.en: Let's take a look at our final phrase.
So when I say get a load of something, I mean look at, right?
transcript.zh: 当我说 get a load of something，意思就是「看看」，对吧？

transcript.en: Get a load of this guy.
Yeah, that's what we heard in the dialogue.
transcript.zh: 对，这就是我们在对话中听到的。

transcript.en: Now, you can use this phrase in a number of different ways and we have some examples for you.
transcript.zh: 这个短语可以有多种用法，我们有一些例子给大家。

transcript.en: A war has started in Antarctica.
Get a load of that house.
Okay, I think we've covered a lot of interesting words and phrases, so we are ready to listen to our dialogue a second time.
transcript.zh: 好的，我想我们已经讲了很多有趣的词汇和短语，准备好听第二遍对话了。

transcript.en: But this time it's going to be a little bit slower so we can pick up all these great words.
transcript.zh: 但这次会慢一点，这样我们就能听清所有这些很棒的词。

transcript.en: Okay, so we noticed some really great words and phrases and with this, now we can start with some Fluency Builder.
transcript.zh: 好的，我们注意到了一些非常好的词汇和短语，现在可以开始流利表达了。

transcript.en: Today, on Fluency Builder, we have two great phrases that you can use to sound a little bit more natural when you speak.
transcript.zh: 今天的流利表达，我们有两个很棒的短语，用了能让你的口语听起来更自然。

transcript.en: Our first phrase you can use if you want to say, don't speak to me like that.
transcript.zh: 第一个短语，当你想说「别这样跟我说话」时可以用。

transcript.en: Don't take that tone with me.
transcript.zh: 别用那种口气跟我说话。

transcript.en: Don't take that tone with me.
transcript.zh: Don't take that tone with me.

transcript.en: So you often hear this phrase coming out of the mouth of a mother or a father.
transcript.zh: 你经常能从父母嘴里听到这个短语。

transcript.en: Yeah, when their children are maybe talking back.
transcript.zh: 是的，当他们的孩子顶嘴的时候。

transcript.en: Don't take that tone with me, young man.
transcript.zh: 别用那种口气跟我说话，小伙子。

transcript.en: I used to get that a lot.
Okay, our second phrase, we use it when we have a problem.
transcript.zh: 好的，第二个短语，当我们遇到问题时使用。

transcript.en: The phrase we heard in the dialogue was, I think we've got ourselves a situation here.
transcript.zh: 我们在对话中听到的短语是：I think we've got ourselves a situation here。

transcript.en: Houston, we've got ourselves a situation here.
transcript.zh: 休斯顿，我们这儿有个情况。

transcript.en: Houston, we've got ourselves a situation here.
transcript.zh: Houston, we've got ourselves a situation here.

transcript.en: Sometimes I use this phrase when I want to tell my boss that I have a problem.
transcript.zh: 有时候我想告诉老板我有个问题时，会用这个短语。

transcript.en: I might say, boss, I've got a bit of a situation.
transcript.zh: 我可能会说，老板，我这儿有点状况。

transcript.en: Can you help me with it?
Yeah, I have a little bit of a problem.
So now we can listen to our dialogue a final time and this time we can understand everything that's in it.
transcript.zh: 现在我们可以最后听一遍对话了，这次我们能完全理解里面的所有内容。

I'm pretty happy we had a song to play there instead of us having to sing.

dialogue.en: A: I hate working on Christmas Eve!
A: Whoa!
A: Get a load of this guy!
A: Come in central, I think we've got ourselves a situation here.

dialogue.en: B: License and registration please.
B: Have you been drinking tonight, sir?

B: Sir, what do you have in the back?
dialogue.zh: B：先生，你后座装的是什么？

dialogue.en: A: Just a few Christmas gifts, 'tis the season, after all!
dialogue.zh: A：只是一些圣诞礼物，毕竟，这是送礼的季节嘛！

dialogue.en: B: Don't take that tone with me.

dialogue.en: A: Umm...no... I make these in my workshop in the North Pole!
dialogue.zh: A：嗯…没有…这些是我在北极的作坊里做的！

dialogue.en: B: You are under arrest, sir.
B: You have the right to remain silent.
